primary.summary: Liquidation/short-squeeze reversal: continuously score wipeout intensity (extreme range + volume spike + OI collapse) across the top-40 and trade the 1-3 day snap-back of the overshoot.
primary.mechanism: Forced deleveraging is mechanical, price-insensitive flow: when a leveraged crowd is stopped out, cascading liquidation market orders push price beyond any information-justified level, visible at the 8h close as extreme range, volume spikes, and OI collapse. The overshoot snaps back over the following 1-3 days as liquidity providers and value-sensitive flow re-enter, and post-cascade funding flips toward paying the reversal side (negative after long-wipeouts), so the engine's native funding stream is a tailwind rather than a drag. Implemented as a continuous cross-sectional flush/squeeze-intensity score with always-ranked tails (price/volume fallback where OI is NaN pre-2020-09), so breadth holds even in quiet weeks.
primary.falsifier: If names ranked by flush/squeeze intensity show no positive net IS Sharpe at 1x costs on the snap-back over any 1-9 candle holding horizon - or the effect exists only pre-cost - the family is dead.

backups.summary: Short-horizon cross-sectional reversal: fade 1-3 day relative overreaction within the top-40, with turnover-controlled smoothed ranks.
backups.mechanism: Crypto's retail-dominated cross-section overreacts at 1-3 day horizons: attention-driven chasing pushes relative winners too far and panic selling pushes relative losers too far, and with no short-horizon fundamental anchor those relative moves mean-revert as the aggressive flow exhausts. The fade is cross-sectionally hedged, so it pays in bull, bear, and chop alike; the design problem is turnover discipline (rank smoothing, tail holding, partial rebalancing) so the edge survives 8h-cadence taker fees plus slippage.
backups.falsifier: If the 1-3 day reversal spread's net IS Sharpe at 1x costs is <= 0 for every turnover-controlled variant (a pre-cost edge that cannot be captured after costs counts as dead), the family is dead.

backups.summary: Dispersion/correlation-regime conditioning: trade the relative-value cross-section as noise-fade when pairwise correlation is high (macro regime) and as persistence when correlation is low (idiosyncratic regime).
backups.mechanism: When trailing pairwise correlation across the top-40 is high, a single macro factor dominates and relative moves are mostly noise that mean-reverts; when correlation is low, capital is rotating on coin-specific narratives and relative moves persist. Conditioning the sign and sizing of the cross-section on the observable correlation regime harvests the same relative-value spread in the manner matched to the regime that generated it - the registered mechanism is the correlation-regime conditioning itself, not any unconditional momentum or reversal signal.
backups.falsifier: If correlation-regime-conditioned variants show neither positive net IS Sharpe at 1x costs nor improvement over their best unconditional counterpart (the conditioning adds nothing), the family is dead.
